subject: Re: Prepay drawdown structure and ramp cadence clarifications
messages:
From: A. Patel <ap@dataforge.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@datacorp.com
Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Prepay drawdown structure — follow-up from pricing call

Laura —

Thanks again for the call this morning. A few follow-ups from our side after reviewing the draft SOW and the wallet/drawdown examples you shared: 1) We want a predictable monthly drawdown schedule for year 1 with the ability to accelerate usage into a prepay bucket if we exceed expectations; 2) We'd prefer a tiered discount that scales with cumulative spend across the commitment term; 3) Need clarity on how unused prepay balances roll forward between years and any true‑up mechanisms at renewal.

Attached is our internal prepay requirements doc (short). Can you propose a playbook or sample cadence (quarterly vs monthly drawdown) and indicate where Redwood would apply price breaks vs. absolute committed units? Also flag any operational constraints around refunds, credits, and reporting cadence.

Best,
A. (Amit) Patel
Head of Procurement, DataForge
attachments: DataForge_requirements.pdf (pdf)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: A. Patel <ap@dataforge.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 May 2025 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prepay drawdown structure — follow-up from pricing call

Amit —

Thanks for the succinct list. I pulled our standard prepay playbook and sketched a tailored ladder for DataForge. High level proposal below; I attached a worked example (redwood-prepay-ladder-2025.xlsx) and an updated SOW with the wallet language (DataForge_SOW_v2.pdf).

Summary proposal (draft):
- Year 1 (annual prepay): Customer prepays a USD 600k wallet covering token/embeddings usage.
- Drawdown cadence: monthly baseline drawdown of USD 40k (12x), with an acceleration trigger: if monthly consumption > 130% of baseline for two consecutive months, the wallet supports on-demand drawdown (no extra charge beyond tokens) but triggers a quarterly review and potential top-up.
- Tiered discounts: 0–600k: list price; 600k–1.2M cumulative across term: 7% discount; >1.2M: 12% discount (discounts apply to subsequent months once thresholds are hit).
- Yearly true-up: any unused prepay after Year 1 can be rolled to Year 2 up to 20% of Year 1 committed amount; amounts above that are credited at 50% of list.
- Ops & reporting: daily token usage ping + monthly ledger export; finance will receive a monthly reconciliation CSV.

Open items where I need alignment from you: preferred drawdown cadence (monthly vs quarterly), tolerance for roll-forward credits, and whether you require a carve-out for evaluation/test environments.

Internal note: karthik/ben — please review the discount breakpoints and confirm margin impact and whether we can flex the roll‑forward credit from 50% to 65% in special cases.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Director, Commercial & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-prepay-ladder-2025.xlsx (xlsx), DataForge_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prepay drawdown structure — internal pricing review

Laura —

Quick pricing read: the proposed breakpoints are reasonable vs comparable deals but two asks: 1) Move the first discount (7%) to kick in at 800k cumulative instead of 600k to preserve initial margin cushion; 2) Keep the 12% for >1.2M but require a 30-day advance notification for applying the higher tier (so accounting has time to adjust).

On credits: switching roll-forward above 20% to 65% is expensive. I recommend we offer 40% roll-forward credit for >80% committed renewal, otherwise keep the 50% default. That gives us flexibility to negotiate during renewal.

Operationally: monthly drawdown is easier for ledgering. Quarterly drawdown adds complexity to our billing export and reduces transparency for customers. Recommend sticking to monthly but allowing a quarterly billing consolidation if DataForge requests it.

Ben — any legal flags on the notification window?

-Karthik
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prepay drawdown structure — legal/ops comments

All —

From a contracting perspective: 1) Notification windows are fine but put them in the SOW as an "eligibility" clause rather than an automatic retroactive rebate; eligibility is evaluated at the time of the tier upgrade. 2) For roll‑forward credits, we should avoid hard cash refunds — credits only. 3) Add a clause that test/dev projects are capped at 5% of committed units unless explicitly carved out in writing.

I'll update the SOW language to reflect these points; Laura, I can push a redline by Friday.

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: A. Patel <ap@dataforge.com>, emma@dataforge.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prepay drawdown structure — final proposal + next steps

Amit / Emma —

Thanks for the patience while we pulled the playbook together. Attached are the updated SOW and the worked ladder with the changes Karthik and Ben recommended. Quick summary of the final proposal: 1) USD 600k Year 1 prepay wallet; monthly baseline drawdown of USD 40k; acceleration triggers at 130% for two consecutive months with on‑demand drawdown supported; 2) Revised discount breakpoints: 7% at 800k cumulative, 12% at >1.2M with a 30‑day eligibility notice; 3) Roll‑forward: up to 20% carries at 50% credit; at renewal if DataForge re-commits at >=80% of prior year, we will increase the carry credit to 40% (not cash); 4) Test/dev cap at 5% of committed units.

Please confirm acceptance of the approach and if acceptable we will: a) issue a redlined SOW (Ben will attach), b) issue a draft order form with PO language, and c) schedule a 30‑minute ops handoff to run through the monthly ledger and reporting exports.

If you agree, please reply with a one-line confirmation and attach your PO when ready.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Director, Commercial & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
attachments: DataForge_SOW_v2_redline.pdf (pdf), redwood-prepay-ladder-2025.xlsx (xlsx)
From: emma@dataforge.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: ap@dataforge.com, procurement@datacorp.com
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 16:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prepay drawdown structure — final proposal + next steps

Laura —

Thanks — that all looks fine to us. We appreciate the flexibility on the discount breakpoint and the renewal carry uplift. Please send the redline and order form; I'll attach PO-DF-114 once the order form has standard PO language (we expect to sign this week).

One small request: can the ops handoff be scheduled for Tue or Wed next week (US Pacific morning)? That timing works best for our integration team.

Emma
VP, Cloud Ops, DataForge
attachments: PO-DF-114.pdf (pdf)
